## The question

[Height Of A Vector Respect To A SubSpace](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/4186563/height-of-a-vector-respect-to-a-subspace), asked by [user232560](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/890400/user232560) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2021-06-30; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> Can anyone explain me what means the following: 
>
> To compute the volume of a $n$ dimensional parallelepiped we use the base x height rule, we pick a vector, then height is the distance from this vector to the subspace spanned by the remainimg vectors,  where base is the $(n-1)$ dimensional volume formed by the remaining vectors.
>
> ¿What means height there?, I  understand it with $2$, $3$ dimensions, but what about 4?
:::

Like it says:

> height is the distance from this vector to the subspace spanned by the remainimg vectors

If the vectors are $v_1, v_2, \dots, v_n$, then $v_1,v_2,\dots,v_{n-1}$ span a subspace $W$.  The distance from $v_n$ to $W$ is the minimum length of all vectors $v_n - w$, as $w$ ranges over $W$.

It's unlikely you would need to compute this height directly.  Most of the time the volume of a parallelepiped would be computed using the determinant formula.
